correctness.rationale: After translating one singleton label to zero, let A be the n labels in the large part and z the other singleton. Every element of -A and z-A is an edge difference, while every nonzero difference in A-A is a nonedge difference. The induced-embedding criterion therefore makes A-A disjoint from both translates. If -a=z-b, then z=b-a is simultaneously the singleton-edge difference and a nonedge difference inside A, so the two translates are also disjoint. Since |A-A|>=n and each translate has n elements, every host has at least 3n elements. The explicit host Z_3 x Z_n with all nonzero first-coordinate differences is K_{n,n,n} and contains the required induced K_{1,1,n}. The universal argument does not rely on the finite verifier.
risks: The claim uses the exact edge/nonedge signed-difference characterization from the initiating eta paper; that criterion was treated as a cited premise and its use here was checked carefully.
